meta_desc: Step-by-step NCERT Class 12 Maths Exercise 3.4 solutions: finding the inverse of a matrix by elementary operations, plus a free 8-question quiz to try.

quiz.title: Inverse by Elementary Operations Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on elementary row and column operations and finding A inverse by the A = IA method. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Matrices Exercise 3.4 — inverse of a matrix by elementary operations

questions.q: In the elementary transformation method, to find the inverse of A you begin by writing which equation?
questions.explanation: The row-operation method starts from A = IA. You then apply row operations to reduce the left A to I, and the same operations turn the right I into A inverse.

questions.q: When finding the inverse using row operations from A = IA, on which matrices must each operation be applied?
options: Only on the left matrix A
On A and simultaneously on the I to its right
On A and on the answer at the end
questions.explanation: Every row operation is applied to A on the left AND to the identity matrix on the right at the same time, so the equality is preserved throughout.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid elementary row operation?
options: Adding a constant to every entry of a row
questions.explanation: The three elementary operations are interchanging two rows, multiplying a row by a non-zero scalar, and adding a multiple of one row to another. Interchange is one of them.

questions.q: For the inverse to exist by elementary operations, the matrix A must be
questions.explanation: Only a non-singular matrix, one whose determinant is non-zero, has an inverse. If A is singular no sequence of elementary operations can reduce it to I.

questions.q: While reducing A to I by row operations, if all the entries of one row of A become zero, this means
options: A inverse equals that zero row
You must switch to column operations
questions.explanation: A full zero row shows A is singular, so the inverse does not exist. NCERT notes this as the signal to stop.

questions.q: If you choose column operations, which equation should you start from?
questions.explanation: Column operations use A = AI. You reduce the left A to I using column operations, applying each to the I on the right, which becomes A inverse.

questions.q: The notation R1 to R1 - 2R2 means
options: Replace row 1 with row 1 minus twice row 2
questions.explanation: It is the operation 'add a multiple of one row to another': the new row 1 is the old row 1 minus 2 times row 2. Row 2 itself is unchanged.

questions.q: In a single derivation of A inverse, NCERT advises that you should
options: Mix row and column operations freely
Use only row operations or only column operations, not both
Use row operations only for 2x2 matrices
questions.explanation: You must apply either row operations throughout or column operations throughout in one derivation. Mixing the two in the same process is not valid.

faq.q: What does Exercise 3.4 of NCERT Class 12 Matrices cover?
faq.a: It covers finding the inverse of a square matrix using elementary transformations — the elementary row operations and column operations — rather than the adjoint or determinant formula. You practise the A = IA method until A reduces to the identity.

faq.q: How do you find the inverse of a matrix by elementary row operations?
faq.a: Write A = IA. Apply elementary row operations to the A on the left to reduce it step by step to the identity matrix, applying the exact same operation to the I on the right each time. When the left side becomes I, the right side is A inverse.

faq.q: Can I mix row and column operations while finding one inverse?
faq.a: No. In a single derivation you use either row operations throughout (starting from A = IA) or column operations throughout (starting from A = AI). Mixing the two in the same process gives a wrong result.

faq.q: What happens if a whole row or column becomes zero during the process?
faq.a: If every entry of a row (or column) turns to zero before you reach the identity, the matrix is singular and its inverse does not exist. That zero line is the signal to stop.
